interpretations.rationale: State of this run. Asserted, each scoped to its executed basis: (1) a follower that has installed a snapshot for (L,T) but still advertises an earlier term for index L rejects the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T (retained CheckRun 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1, indices 5 and 6 against control 1 and 2); (2) with TrailingLogs=0 and a snapshot taken at the log end, the leader cannot repair such a follower - it re-sends the whole snapshot while the follower's applied index stays at the snapshot index (single-peer witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7, indices 3 and 1; sealed-partition witness on a produced five-node history CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30, indices 1, 2 and 9); (3) the load-bearing difference for the non-zero-TrailingLogs cases is how much of its log the leader retains below the snapshot index at snapshot time (control CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f, indices 9 and 19). Narrowed and partly refuted along the way: an earlier negative reading of the five-node history was an artifact of an incomplete partition and its Fact was revised in place; the generalisation that any non-zero TrailingLogs merely delays the loop was refuted (CheckRun 0b99df9ed72e4cd2b653c5741e4eec3d); and the further generalisation that the compacted-boundary condition is sufficient was refuted by the backlog case in the same receipt family (CheckRun 62f089bd843641099558ff8d8831ab29, indices 35 and 43). For a human reviewer the defensible statement is therefore: with TrailingLogs=0 and a snapshot taken at the log end, a rejoining follower can be unrepairable and the leader loops on whole-snapshot transfers; with non-zero TrailingLogs the executed histories converge, and the compaction condition does not by itself predict the loop. Still open: (a) the mechanism by which the backlog-case peer was repaired - its store ended at 61..62 while the leader's was 63..64 at the same applied index 64 and it had applied 61 commands, which is consistent with the peer snapshotting on its own under the shared small SnapshotThreshold and is not isolated; (b) whether the default TrailingLogs (10240) with a matching backlog reproduces the loop, which was never executed; (c) the older registered gaps that this run answered only in prose, because their investigation ids were not resolvable for formal answers. One record inconsistency should be read with this entry: 7465f7b9e6cd44e39e8cbf7e2c45c955-interpretation-0 still reads as refuting the loop for the five-node history, but its Fact was revised (revision 2) and the lineage entry 059c0fbb2e8849188bb09529ad9118a8-interpretation-0 explains that the refutation applied only to the incomplete-partition harness.

investigations.question: After a follower successfully installs an InstallSnapshot whose last included entry is (index L, term T), must the follower accept the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L and PrevLogTerm=T, and does it still do so when the follower already held a log entry at L from an earlier term?
investigations.hypothesis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot but never calls setLastLog nor invalidates the pre-existing log entry at L. getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, so once the snapshot makes lastSnapshotIndex == L while the stale log entry keeps lastLogIndex == L, the tie is resolved in favour of the stale log term. The follower's PrevLogEntry==L check then compares the leader's snapshot term T against the stale term and answers Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true. The leader sets nextIndex = max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1), which lands on L; setPreviousLog(L) then needs the leader's own log entry L-1, which is absent once the leader has compacted up to its snapshot index (compactLogsWithTrailing can leave firstIndex > L-1), so replicateTo jumps to SEND_SNAP, re-sends the same snapshot, restores nextIndex=L+1, and the same rejection recurs.
investigations.discriminator: Drive one node with real RPCs: bootstrap it as a Nonvoter, seed a command at index 2 with an AppendEntries whose Term is 2, install an InstallSnapshot with LastLogIndex=2 and LastLogTerm=3, then send AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3. The necessary property is met only if the last append succeeds; the suspicion holds if it fails while an otherwise identical control node without the seeded entry succeeds. Refuted if the post-snapshot append succeeds in both cases, or if getLastEntry reports the snapshot term for index 2.

knowledge.statement: On accepting an InstallSnapshot, installSnapshot sets lastApplied=req.LastLogIndex and lastSnapshot=(req.LastLogIndex,req.LastLogTerm), restores latest and committed configuration from the snapshot payload, then clears the log store (removeOldLogs) for a monotonic store or compacts it (compactLogs(req.LastLogIndex)) otherwise, and finally sets resp.Success=true. It never calls setLastLog and never truncates a pre-existing log suffix at or above req.LastLogIndex, so lastLogIndex keeps its pre-snapshot value and a stale entry at the snapshot index can remain in the store.
knowledge.conditions: Reached only when the RPC header passes checkRPCHeader, the snapshot version is supported, req.Term >= currentTerm, the snapshot bytes are fully received (n == req.Size) and the FSM restore succeeds.

knowledge.statement: raftState.getLastIndex returns max(lastLogIndex,lastSnapshotIndex) and getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, otherwise (lastSnapshotIndex,lastSnapshotTerm). The comparison is on index only, so when the two sources name the same index with different terms the log-derived term wins. appendEntries uses this as the PrevLogEntry==lastIdx fast path and otherwise reads logs.GetLog(PrevLogEntry); a term mismatch or a missing entry yields Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any *Raft whose log and snapshot were written by different ingest paths (NewRaft startup restore, installSnapshot, takeSnapshot, liveBootstrap, dispatchLogs, AppendEntries append, restoreUserSnapshot).

A snapshot is taken at the FSM's applied index, so in a quiet cluster snapshotIndex is close to lastLogIdx and the deletion stops well below the snapshot index, leaving the leader able to serve entries below its snapshot boundary. The leader's retained first index passes the snapshot index only when lastLogIdx - trailingLogs >= snapshotIndex at snapshot time, i.e. when the log end is at least TrailingLogs ahead of the snapshot index when the snapshot is taken. history.correction: Extended from source arithmetic to measured confirmation, and the earlier reading that a nonzero TrailingLogs merely delays the loop is corrected: a snapshot taken while the log end is only marginally ahead of the snapshot index compacts nothing at all, so the loop does not occur at any trailing value unless the log end has outgrown the snapshot index by at least TrailingLogs at snapshot time.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes a necessary property and a mechanism that appears to violate it. Property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L,T), a node's state at L is the snapshot's, so the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T must be accepted. Mechanism: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but leaves lastLogIndex and any stale log entry at L untouched; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, i.e. precisely the tie produced when the follower already held an entry at L from an earlier term; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1500) then reports Success=false, NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader side (replication.go 223, 256, 286-300, 370): nextIndex becomes L via max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); setPreviousLog(L) requires the leader's entry L-1; once the leader has compacted past L (compactLogsWithTrailing can set firstIndex > L-1) that lookup returns ErrLogNotFound, which routes to SEND_SNAP and re-installs the same snapshot. Local construction feedback (harness assurance_generated_test.go, both sub-cases, run in a scratch copy) matched the prediction exactly: with the stale same-index entry, state_after_snapshot reported last_log_index=2/last_log_term=2 against last_snapshot_index=2/last_snapshot_term=3 and the follow-up append returned success=false/no_retry_backoff=true; without the seeded entry the same append returned success=true. The consolidation records what stands asserted, each on its executed basis: a follower that installed a snapshot for (L,T) yet advertises an earlier term for L rejects the leader boundary append (CheckRun 72367650c8d0470d8197a7d2c0f97ce1); with TrailingLogs=0 and a snapshot taken at the log end the leader cannot repair such a follower and re-sends the whole snapshot while the follower applied index stays pinned at the snapshot index (single-peer witness CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7 and sealed-partition witness CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30, cause isolated by control CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f). It also records what was refuted or narrowed (the incomplete-partition artifact with its in-place Fact revision, the claim that non-zero TrailingLogs merely delays the loop, and the sufficiency of the compaction condition) and what remains open (the backlog peer unexplained repair path, plausibly its own snapshotting under the shared small SnapshotThreshold; the default TrailingLogs case with a matching backlog, never executed; and the older registered gaps answered only in prose because their ids were not resolvable for formal answers). It flags one record inconsistency for reviewers: 7465f7b9e6cd44e39e8cbf7e2c45c955-interpretation-0 still reads as refuting the loop for the five-node history, while its Fact was revised and the lineage entry 059c0fbb2e8849188bb09529ad9118a8-interpretation-0 explains that the refutation applied only to the incomplete-partition harness, which left the partner reachable from the majority. The honest limits are stated: only TrailingLogs=0 with a snapshot taken at the log end has a demonstrated unrepairable-follower loop, all evidence is in-process five-node with in-memory transports and stores on frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df, and human review owns final defect validity, CFT relevance and deduplication. investigations.question: After a follower successfully installs an InstallSnapshot whose last included entry is (index L, term T), must the follower accept the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L and PrevLogTerm=T, and does it still do so when the follower already held a log entry at L from an earlier term?
investigations.hypothesis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot but never calls setLastLog nor invalidates the pre-existing log entry at L. getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, so once the snapshot makes lastSnapshotIndex == L while the stale log entry keeps lastLogIndex == L, the tie is resolved in favour of the stale log term. The follower's PrevLogEntry==L check then compares the leader's snapshot term T against the stale term and answers Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true. The leader sets nextIndex = max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1), which lands on L; setPreviousLog(L) then needs the leader's own log entry L-1, which is absent once the leader has compacted up to its snapshot index (compactLogsWithTrailing can leave firstIndex > L-1), so replicateTo jumps to SEND_SNAP, re-sends the same snapshot, restores nextIndex=L+1, and the same rejection recurs.
investigations.discriminator: Drive one node with real RPCs: bootstrap it as a Nonvoter, seed a command at index 2 with an AppendEntries whose Term is 2, install an InstallSnapshot with LastLogIndex=2 and LastLogTerm=3, then send AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=2/PrevLogTerm=3. The necessary property is met only if the last append succeeds; the suspicion holds if it fails while an otherwise identical control node without the seeded entry succeeds. Refuted if the post-snapshot append succeeds in both cases, or if getLastEntry reports the snapshot term for index 2.

knowledge.statement: On accepting an InstallSnapshot, installSnapshot sets lastApplied=req.LastLogIndex and lastSnapshot=(req.LastLogIndex,req.LastLogTerm), restores latest and committed configuration from the snapshot payload, then clears the log store (removeOldLogs) for a monotonic store or compacts it (compactLogs(req.LastLogIndex)) otherwise, and finally sets resp.Success=true. It never calls setLastLog and never truncates a pre-existing log suffix at or above req.LastLogIndex, so lastLogIndex keeps its pre-snapshot value and a stale entry at the snapshot index can remain in the store.
knowledge.conditions: Reached only when the RPC header passes checkRPCHeader, the snapshot version is supported, req.Term >= currentTerm, the snapshot bytes are fully received (n == req.Size) and the FSM restore succeeds.

knowledge.statement: raftState.getLastIndex returns max(lastLogIndex,lastSnapshotIndex) and getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, otherwise (lastSnapshotIndex,lastSnapshotTerm). The comparison is on index only, so when the two sources name the same index with different terms the log-derived term wins. appendEntries uses this as the PrevLogEntry==lastIdx fast path and otherwise reads logs.GetLog(PrevLogEntry); a term mismatch or a missing entry yields Success=false with NoRetryBackoff=true.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any *Raft whose log and snapshot were written by different ingest paths (NewRaft startup restore, installSnapshot, takeSnapshot, liveBootstrap, dispatchLogs, AppendEntries append, restoreUserSnapshot).

knowledge.statement: On a rejected AppendEntries the leader rewinds the follower's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1); when that lands on the follower's snapshot boundary L and the leader's own log has been compacted so that L-1 is no longer stored, the rebuild of the request returns ErrLogNotFound, which replicateTo maps to SEND_SNAP. sendLatestSnapshot then ships the current snapshot and, on success, sets nextIndex = meta.Index+1 = L+1, so the following append again carries PrevLogEntry=L. interpretations.rationale: Source establishes a necessary property and a mechanism that appears to violate it. Property: after a successful InstallSnapshot for (L,T), a node's state at L is the snapshot's, so the leader's next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=L/PrevLogTerm=T must be accepted. Mechanism: installSnapshot (raft.go 1814-1953) sets lastSnapshot=(L,T) but leaves lastLogIndex and any stale log entry at L untouched; getLastEntry (state.go 167-174) prefers the log term whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, i.e. precisely the tie produced when the follower already held an entry at L from an earlier term; appendEntries (raft.go 1475-1500) then reports Success=false, NoRetryBackoff=true. Leader side (replication.go 223, 256, 286-300, 370): nextIndex becomes L via max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); setPreviousLog(L) requires the leader's entry L-1; once the leader has compacted past L (compactLogsWithTrailing can set firstIndex > L-1) that lookup returns ErrLogNotFound, which routes to SEND_SNAP and re-installs the same snapshot. Local construction feedback (harness assurance_generated_test.go, both sub-cases, run in a scratch copy) matched the prediction exactly: with the stale same-index entry, state_after_snapshot reported last_log_index=2/last_log_term=2 against last_snapshot_index=2/last_snapshot_term=3 and the follow-up append returned success=false/no_retry_backoff=true; without the seeded entry the same append returned success=true. That run is not a retained receipt, so the defect claim is left unresolved pending the controller's execution of the registered experiment; the leader-side loop of the gap above is likewise still unexecuted.
counterevidence: Behind-follower case does not trigger it: when the follower's lastLogIndex is below the snapshot index, getLastEntry returns the snapshot pair and the appended entries are accepted (observed as the harness control: last_log_index=1 < last_snapshot_index=2 -> success=true).

With the default TrailingLogs the leader normally retains entries below its snapshot index, so setPreviousLog(L) succeeds, the leader backs off one index and appendEntries truncates the conflicting suffix from its stored copy, converging without a snapshot loop; the loop needs the leader to have compacted up to or past L.

Circumstances: legal trigger is AddVoter(server-B) on a leader whose retained log begins above snapshot index L=8; observation interval is 300 ms and 1500 ms after the call, under no injected faults, no partitions and a responsive transport. Repeated nonprogress: across that 1.2 s window the peer received roughly 13.4 thousand additional InstallSnapshot deliveries and its applied index did not move off the snapshot index at all.
